title: The Sting
tagline: ...all it takes is a little Confidence.
about: Two Chicago grifters in 1936 set up a fake betting parlour to take a vicious mob boss for half a million.
cue: Serve the prime rib when Lonnegan puts it all on Lucky Dan.

Apple and celery with walnuts in creamy dressing.How to make it2 red apples, diced3 celery sticks, sliced1 cup red grapes, halved80g walnuts4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise3 tbsp Greek yoghurt1 lemon1 butter lettuce, leaves separatedToast the walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant and roughly chop.Whisk the mayo, yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon with salt and pepper.Toss the apple, celery and grapes through the dressing.Pile onto the lettuce leaves and scatter with walnuts.Four-threes crab cakesFloyd swears he dealt Shaw four threes. Golden crab cakes with lemon remoulade.How to make it400g cooked crab meat60g panko breadcrumbs, plus 60g for coating1 egg3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise, plus 4 tbsp for the remoulade1 tsp Dijon mustard2 spring onions, sliced1 tbsp capers, chopped1 tbsp chopped gherkins1 lemon4 tbsp vegetable oilMix the crab, 60g panko, egg, 3 tbsp mayo, mustard and spring onions and shape 12 small cakes.Coat in the rest of the panko and chill for 10 minutes.Fry in the oil until golden on both sides.Stir the rest of the mayo with the capers, gherkins and lemon and serve alongside.EntreesLucky Dan roast prime ribPlace it on Lucky Dan. Rare rib roast with horseradish cream and jus.How to make it2kg beef rib roast, 2 bones2 tbsp olive oil3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp thyme leaves250ml beef stock150ml sour cream2 tbsp grated horseradish800g small potatoesRub the beef with the oil, garlic, thyme and plenty of salt and pepper.Roast on the potatoes at 230°C for 20 minutes, then at 160°C until rare in the middle.Rest the beef under foil and keep the potatoes warm.Deglaze the tin with the stock for a jus and stir the horseradish into the sour cream.Carve thick slices and serve with the potatoes, jus and horseradish cream.Lonnegan's packing house pork chopsLonnegan owns a packing house. Thick pork chops with mustard apples.How to make it4 thick bone-in pork chops2 tbsp olive oil30g butter2 green apples, cut in wedges1 brown onion, sliced200ml cloudy apple juice1 tbsp wholegrain mustard2 sage sprigsSeason the chops and sear in the oil until deep golden on both sides and just cooked, then rest.Melt the butter and fry the apples, onion and sage until caramelised.Add the apple juice and mustard and bubble until glossy.Return the chops with their juices and spoon the apples over.DessertsLoretta's diner apple pieLoretta is only filling in for June. Warm double-crust apple pie with vanilla ice cream.How to make it2 sheets of shortcrust pastry6 Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced100g brown sugar1 tbsp cornflour1 tsp ground cinnamon20g butter, diced1 egg, beaten500ml vanilla ice creamLine a pie dish with one sheet of pastry.Toss the apples with the sugar, cornflour and cinnamon, pile into the case and dot with butter.Lay over the second sheet, crimp, cut steam holes and brush with egg.Bake at 190°C until golden and bubbling, then rest.Serve warm with ice cream.BeveragesGin with the markAlways drink gin with the mark. London dry gin and tonic with a lime wedge.How to make it240ml London dry gin800ml tonic water, chilled2 limes, cut in wedges2 cups ice cubesFill 4 tumblers with ice and pour 60ml gin into each.Top with tonic and squeeze in a lime wedge.Black coffee for Mr. LonneganThe name's Lonnegan.
